title: Toki
build: Ocean type 1 cartridge, 16 banks of 8 KB (128 KB)

records.c: The first 11 bytes of Stage 5's data block, loaded from $0C01. Bytes 2-4 are the stage's three background colours ($D021-$D023; stage_setup_tables copies them to bg_colour0-2): 00, 08, 0C here. Byte 5 (07) is the number of the last section, which track_stage_section and init_round_state read. Bytes 6-7 ($8892) point into cartridge bank 0 to the 64 bytes of stream records that load_stage_bank_records copies to $0100. Bytes 8-9 ($89C3) point to the list of animation ids that the helper at $06E6 searches, and byte 10 (33) is that list's last index. Bytes 0 and 1 (79, 4C) are read by nothing in play.

The 22 bytes $0C0C-$0C21 are Stage 5's eleven table pointers; stage_setup_tables copies them to $2A-$3F (map_row_lo_ptr, map_row_hi_ptr, block_chars_ptr, block_props_ptr, path_table_ptr, $34, script_ptr_a, script_ptr_b, anim_lo_ptr, anim_hi_ptr and $3E). Their values here are $1BB9, $1C05, $0D32, $1B6E, $1D18, $1D21, $2007, $2024, $1FCB, $1F97, $1FFF.

Colour of each character code in Stage 5, 256 bytes, indexed by the character (screen code) found in the screen buffers. recolour_screen copies the entry for every one of the 840 playfield characters into colour RAM. Only the low nibble reaches colour RAM, and a value of 8 or more turns on multicolour for that character, since the playfield runs in multicolour text mode ($D016 bit 4).

Table of section record addresses for Stage 5: one word for each of its 8 sections, $0D22-$0D31, starting $1C51, $1C6A, $1C83 and on, each 25 bytes on. store_section_index indexes it with section_index times 2, track_stage_section with the next and the previous section's index times 2, and init_round_state with the last section's ($0C06); stage_setup_tables reads the first word through $24.

The map block table of Stage 5: four screen characters for each of 75 block numbers (upper left, upper right, lower left, lower right), $0D32-$0E5D, pointed to by block_chars_ptr ($2E). The table's length depends on the stage.

The block numbers of Stage 5's map, one byte for each block position, from $0E5E to $1B6D. map_row_lo/hi_table give each of the 76 rows' start (first $0E24, $0E63, $0EA2); rows differ in length, and a row's pointer is biased by the row's first column, so the byte for block column x is at the row pointer plus x. Each byte indexes block_chars and block_props_table.
Bytes $125E-$165D of map_rows_data ($125E is 1024 bytes in).
Bytes $165E-$1A5D of map_rows_data ($165E is 2048 bytes in).
Bytes $1A5E-$1B6D of map_rows_data ($1A5E is 3072 bytes in).

Map block properties of Stage 5, one byte for each block number: 75 bytes $1B6E-$1BB8, matching the 75 four-character blocks of block_chars ($0D32-$0E5D). block_props_ptr ($30) points here. Bit 0 solid, bit 1 harmful, bits 2 and 3 slopes, bit 5 enter mode 1, as block_property_at and the terrain probes test them. The values present are $00, $01, $02, $10, $11, $20, $30.

Map row address table, low bytes: 76 entries $1BB9-$1C04, one for each row of Stage 5's map. map_row_lo_ptr ($2A) points here and stage_setup_tables copies the pointer from $0C0C. The high bytes are the 76 bytes at $1C05.

Map row address table, high bytes: 76 entries $1C05-$1C50. map_row_hi_ptr ($2C) points here and stage_setup_tables copies the pointer from $0C0E. The low bytes are map_row_lo_table at $1BB9; a row starts at hi:lo.

The 8 section records of Stage 5, 25 bytes each, $1C51-$1D18: section_table ($0D22) holds their addresses. Each record begins with the follow zone (zone_left, zone_right, zone_top, zone_bottom) and the view limits that update_view_scroll reads through section_ptr ($26), and holds the flags byte at offset $16 (section_scroll_flags); the rest of the 25 bytes is not decoded here.

Table of path data addresses that path_table_ptr ($32) points to, indexed by obj_arc_state; the pointer is one below the first entry in the stage 1 table, so the table's first word may start at $1D19. The pointer at $34 is $1D21. The area from $1D19 to $1D20 is 8 bytes; the format of its words is as in stage 1's path_address_table.

The table the pointer at $34 (a copy of $0C16, here $1D21) points to: script command 22 ($B722) reads it through ($34) at $B72D to find the record of an object it sets up. In stage 1 the first path data and these records lie together in this area; where this stage's path data ends is not established.

High bytes of the addresses of Stage 5's animation data blocks, 52 entries $1F97-$1FCA indexed by animation number; anim_hi_ptr ($3C) points here. The low bytes are the 52 bytes of anim_lo_table at $1FCB.
Low bytes of the addresses of Stage 5's animation data blocks, 52 entries $1FCB-$1FFE, indexed by animation number; anim_lo_ptr ($3A) points here. The partner of anim_hi_table.

The eleventh table of Stage 5, which $3E points to (stored by stage_setup_tables from $0C20): the hit reactions 0 and 1 ($A8FA, $A8D8) replace an object's obj_anim_num with the entry at that index, so it maps an animation number to the animation the object switches to when hit. It starts at $1FFF.

Low bytes of the addresses of Stage 5's object movement scripts: 29 entries $2007-$2023, the table that script_ptr_a ($36) points to. object_script_step loads the pair (script_ptr_a, script_ptr_b) into $E3/$E4 and then reads the script byte at ($E3) + obj_script_pos ($379C,x). The high bytes are script_addr_hi.
High bytes of the addresses of Stage 5's object movement scripts: 29 entries $2024-$2040, the table that script_ptr_b ($38) points to; the low bytes are script_addr_lo.

Object movement script bytes of Stage 5, from $2041; the scripts start between $2041 and $21A3. A byte below $80 is a command number: object_script_step looks it up in script_cmd_lo/hi at $B33C/$B35F and runs it; a byte with bit 7 set is a move (low four bits the direction, next byte the repeat count).

Stage 5 entry for table indexes 6, 10, 20, 21 and 25. Calls $B5D5 and resident object_land_bounce ($B4C4); if the carry is set after the bounce it sets obj_state,x=$A0. Entry 22 ($BD86) is not a routine start here: it points into the operand of the lda at $BD84.

Stage 5 entry for table index 26. A hop state machine for one object using obj_off_y,x. If obj_off_y is positive it counts it down and runs stage5_hopper_launch when it reaches 0; if it is 0 it branches to stage5_hopper_airborne; if negative it waits until $E7/$E8 minus player_box_left ($4C/$4D) is below $40 (the object up to 64 pixels right of the player's box), then sets obj_off_y,x=1. Entries 9 ($BDE0) and 24 ($BEB3) point into operands, so they are not routine starts in this stage; 19 ($BDBD) is the start of stage5_hopper_face_player.

Reached from stage5_hopper_step when obj_off_y,x counts down to 0. Takes obj_motion_alt,x & 1 as an index into stage5_hop_counter_table, stores the byte in obj_arc_counter,x, increments obj_motion_alt,x and sets obj_arc_state,x=$80. It then falls into stage5_hopper_face_player.

Stage 5 entry for table index 19, also reached by fall-through from stage5_hopper_launch. It is an instruction start inside the hop routine rather than a separate routine start. Sets bit 0 of obj_state,x, compares $E7/$E8 with the player position (player_x+$1F) and sets obj_dir,x to 7 or $0B, and sets obj_anim_num,x=$2B.

Reached from stage5_hopper_step when obj_off_y,x is 0. Calls $B5D5, then compares $E9/$EA with $0483 and, when the object is low enough, sets obj_off_y,x=$19, clears obj_arc_state,x and bit 0 of obj_state,x and sets obj_anim_num,x=$2B. Otherwise, if bit 6 of obj_arc_state is set it sets obj_anim_num,x=$2C and resets obj_anim_index,x once it reaches 2 (probably the landing animation).
Data, 2 bytes ($40,$60) read as $BE2C,y in stage5_hopper_launch with y = obj_motion_alt,x & 1; stored into obj_arc_counter,x. The disassembly shows rti/rts but these are data.
Stage 5 entry for table index 29. Sets obj_health,x=$5F and returns. Entry 30 ($BE31) points into the operand of the sta at $BE30, so it is not a routine start here.

Stage 5 entry for table index 27. Keeps obj_health,x at $5F. If obj_off_y,x is non-negative it waits for obj_anim_index,x and obj_anim_timer,x to be 0 and then decrements obj_off_y,x; at 0 it sets obj_off_y,x=$FD, obj_arc_state,x=7, obj_arc_counter,x=3 and resets $5F, $63, $67, clearing bit 0 of obj_state,x. If negative and $67 is 0 it increments obj_off_y,x, and at 0 it clears obj_arc_state,x, sets obj_off_y,x=3 and sets bit 0 of obj_state,x. The instruction at $BE73 (table index 7) is an instruction start inside this routine, not a routine start.

Stage 5 entry for table index 28; sets $14=$2C and runs the slide cycle driven by obj_motion_alt,x (0, positive or negative), keeping obj_health,x at $5F. On obj_anim_index,x = 3 with obj_anim_timer,x = 0 it moves $E7/$E8 by $20 right (negative phase, ending at $0750 with obj_off_y,x=$7D) or left (positive phase, sets obj_motion_alt,x=$FF and obj_anim_num,x=$33 when the health low nibble is under 8). Table index 23 ($BE91) is an instruction start inside this routine, after the $14 store.

Reached from the slide cycle when obj_motion_alt,x is 0. Decrements obj_off_y,x; at 0 it increments obj_motion_alt,x, sets bit 0 of obj_state,x, obj_anim_num,x=$31, obj_anim_index,x=3 and obj_health,x=$5F, then returns. Otherwise it ends at the health reset at $BECC.

The character set of the playfield for Stage 5, $C000-$C6A7 (1704 bytes loaded by the stage's character set directory entry): eight pixel rows for each character, starting at character $00 (VIC bank 3, $D018 $21 or $31). stage_load copies it from the cartridge at stage start.
Bytes $C400-$C6A7 of stage_charset ($C400 is 1024 bytes in).
